Estense Campori Soria cc. 9-12.summary: Soria reports that the Genoese commune and its duke, pressed by the French fleet at Savona, will arm galleys if Charles V pays half, and asks Lannoy to send the six imperial galleys at Naples to join the nine at Genoa; a few citizens are talking with the Pope of neutrality, and the League's draft treaty would leave Savona and the riviera to France. Written eight weeks before the Sack of Rome, while Lannoy was negotiating the truce with Clement VII.
Estense Campori Soria cc. 9-12.en:
Most Illustrious and Excellent Lord. The last letter I wrote to Your Illustrious Lordship was of the 23rd of last month, by way of ⟨Ferrara⟩. Captain Bracamonte will carry this one. With him, on the 6th of last month, I received Your Excellency's letter of 3 December, the most recent I have from you, which I have answered in many others. I have told you how the said Bracamonte took on here, with the galleys that went to Corsica, almost all the biscuit he had and the saltpetre, as Your Lordship will see from the certificate he carries of what he has consigned. A little biscuit remained in Corsica, and I have promised that it be sent to me for the provisioning of the galley of the gobo.

Before the said saltpetre arrived I had sent to the Duke of Bourbon, who was near Piacenza, seven mules loaded with cannon powder, and he received it.

system: homophonic letter signs (about 50 types, a few polyvalent) plus a code of three-letter Latin groups (dri que, leb de, den no, lab las, fip galeras, pre Su Magestad) for words and syllables, with frame marks 11, g#, -o-.
